title: Question 1
statement_text: Assuming only that each $a_i \neq 0$, what geometric constraints can be imposed on a set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ which imply non-trivial uniform upper bounds on $\Pr(X \in S)$?
context_text: Here $X=a_1\xi_1+\dots+a_n\xi_n$ where $a_1,\dots,a_n\in\mathbb{R}^d$ are vectors and $\xi_1,\dots,\xi_n$ are i.i.d. Rademacher random variables ($\Pr(\xi_i=1)=\Pr(\xi_i=-1)=1/2$). The classical Erdős–Littlewood–Offord theorem gives $\max_x\Pr(X=x)=O(1/\sqrt{n})$ when every $a_i\neq0$ (and $O(1/\sqrt n)$ for falling in a unit interval when $|a_i|\ge1$, in dimension 1). The paper introduces a new generalisation to $\mathbb{R}^d$: bound $\Pr(X\in S)$ uniformly over all choices of nonzero $a_i$, for a fixed set $S$. Since no assumption is made on the sizes of the $a_i$, the question is much more about the geometry of $S$ than about spatial anti-concentration of $X$; for a smooth manifold $S$ any answer must work both at a local scale (where $S$ looks like an affine subspace) and globally. If $S$ contains a line segment then $\Pr(X\in S)\ge1/2$ is possible, and highly oscillatory sets (such as the graph of $x\mapsto\sin(2\pi x)$) are also obstacles. Costello had shown $\Pr(X\in S)\le n^{-1/2+o(1)}$ for a parabola in $\mathbb{R}^2$. The authors' main answer: if $S$ is definable with respect to an o-minimal structure (for instance any semi-algebraic set, or any set defined by Boolean combinations of equalities and inequalities involving polynomials, the exponential and restricted analytic functions) and contains no line segment, then $\Pr(X\in S)\le n^{-1/2+o(1)}$. This is probability / additive combinatorics rather than graph theory.

title: Conjecture 1.2
statement_text: Let $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ be definable with respect to an o-minimal structure and contain no line segment, and let $X=a_1\xi_1+\dots+a_n\xi_n$ with nonzero $a_1,\dots,a_n\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and i.i.d. Rademacher $\xi_i$. Then $\Pr(X \in S) \leq C_S/\sqrt{n}$, for some $C_S$ depending only on $S$.
context_text: Here $X=a_1\xi_1+\dots+a_n\xi_n$ where $a_1,\dots,a_n\in\mathbb{R}^d$ are vectors and $\xi_1,\dots,\xi_n$ are i.i.d. Rademacher random variables ($\Pr(\xi_i=1)=\Pr(\xi_i=-1)=1/2$). The classical Erdős–Littlewood–Offord theorem gives $\max_x\Pr(X=x)=O(1/\sqrt{n})$ when every $a_i\neq0$ (and $O(1/\sqrt n)$ for falling in a unit interval when $|a_i|\ge1$, in dimension 1). The authors prove: if $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ is definable with respect to an o-minimal structure (this includes every semi-algebraic set, i.e. Boolean combination of polynomial equalities and inequalities, and more generally sets built from polynomials, the exponential and restricted analytic functions) and contains no line segment, then for every $\alpha>0$ and $n$ large enough in terms of $\alpha$ and $S$, every choice of nonzero $a_1,\dots,a_n\in\mathbb{R}^d$ gives $\Pr(X\in S)\le n^{-1/2+\alpha}$. The conjecture asks for the optimal bound $\Pr(X\in S)\le C_S/\sqrt{n}$ in this same setting, matching the Erdős–Littlewood–Offord point-concentration bound. They prove it when $S$ has a generic intersection property, which covers convex or irreducible algebraic plane curves in $\mathbb{R}^2$, irreducible complex algebraic curves in $\mathbb{C}^2\cong\mathbb{R}^4$, and the boundary of a 3-dimensional ball; the simplest open case is the unit 3-sphere in $\mathbb{R}^4$. A full resolution of the Gotsman–Linial conjecture on the average sensitivity of polynomial threshold functions would imply the conjecture for semi-algebraic sets not containing a line segment. This is probability / additive combinatorics rather than graph theory.
